verdict.rationale: PlayCanvas ships AI-oriented documentation: llms.txt, a very large llms-full.txt, and PlayCanvas Skills that give AI coding agents PlayCanvas-specific development and verification workflows. It also documents one component model shared across Editor, Engine, React and Web Components, and is a widely downloaded, versioned npm package. However, nothing shows LLM-generated code actually working on the first try, and the evidence for abundant public training examples is thin. Missing for 10: hands-on evidence of first-try LLM code success, evidence of abundant public example corpora, documentation of API stability or deprecation policy (two scripting styles exist, with ESM only recommended for new projects).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, LLM-generated code mostly works on the first try — stable, well-documented APIs with abundant public examples the models have seen

citations.quote: developer.playcanvas.com serves llms.txt plus the largest llms-full.txt of the arena (2,053,637 bytes of complete docs)
New projects include PlayCanvas Skills, which give compatible AI coding agents PlayCanvas-specific development and verification workflows.
The same components, with the same properties, are available whichever way you build: in the Editor, directly against the engine, in PlayCanvas React and in Web Components.
Use `create-playcanvas` to scaffold a Vite and TypeScript project for the Engine, React, or Web Components from one of 12 runnable starters.
